In the figure there is a straight line slanting downward to the right, passing through the marked points B and A; there is also a straight line slanting upward to the right, marked as y=2x-4. The intersection point of the two straight lines is marked as C. The problem statement gives that the descending straight line y1=kx+b passes through A(5,0) and B(1,4). Reasoning: First find the slope of the straight line y1, k=(4-0)/(1-5)=4/(-4)=-1. Substitute point A(5,0) into y=-x+b, obtaining 0=-5+b, so b=5, therefore y1=-x+5. Point C is the intersection point of y1 and y2=2x-4. Let -x+5=2x-4, obtaining 9=3x, so x=3. Substitute into y=2x-4, obtaining y=2. Therefore the coordinates of C are (3,2).

method.method_draft: Use direct analytic equations.
